cards.explanation: The answer is Galilee, friends. Mark says that after the arrest of John, Jesus went into Galilee and proclaimed the gospel of God (Mark 1:14). John the Baptist had been arrested, and Galilee is where Jesus went next. That's the place Mark names.

The answer is the kingdom of God, friends! Jesus says, "The time is fulfilled…" and "…the kingdom of God is near." (Mark 1:15). He doesn't say it's far off or someday. He says near. That's the kind of news you'd want to hear loud and clear.

The answer is repent and believe in the gospel, friends! Jesus says, "Repent and believe in the gospel!" (Mark 1:15). Two parts, one call. Repent means turning around, and believe means trusting the good news He's announcing.

The answer is fishers of men, friends! Jesus tells Simon and Andrew, "Come, follow Me…" and "…I will make you fishers of men." (Mark 1:17). Simon and Andrew are fishermen, casting a net into the sea, when He says it. I'd have asked what the pay was.

The answer is True, friends! Mark says, "And at once they left their nets and followed Him." (Mark 1:18). Simon and Andrew leave the nets behind and follow. Mark says they do it at once. That's a quick yes.

The answer is mending, friends! Mark says James and John "…were in a boat, mending their nets." (Mark 1:19). They're fixing the tools of their trade when Jesus sees them. Then He calls them right away.

The answer is False, friends. Mark says Jesus called them immediately, and they "…left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed Him." (Mark 1:20). James and John go, and Zebedee stays in the boat.

The answer is the hired men, friends! Mark says James and John left their father Zebedee "…in the boat with the hired men…" (Mark 1:20). So Zebedee isn't left by himself. He has workers right there with him. Hired men, not an empty boat.
